newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares up on first day of BSM trade.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares up on first day of BSM trade.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares rose on Monday -- the first day of trade on the official Beirut Stock exchange (BSE).

A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district which the company is rebuilding, rose to $115.125 from $112.5 on their last closing on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) on Friday.
B shares, issued in a $650 million flotation in January 1994, also rose to $116 at the 0800 gmt fixing from $113.
"The first day went smoothly with no difficulties. Prices have gone up and the volume was good. It was a good day," BSE trading floor chief Fouad Baalbaki told Reuters.
Turnover was 5,352 shares from Friday's 5,226 on the BSM and value was $610,759 compared with $580,192.
There was no trade in any of the four companies listed on the BSM: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
Dealers say the SOLIDERE switch is positive for the development of Lebanon's re-emerging capital markets although it leaves the future of the BSM in doubt.
SOLIDERE's move adds some $2 billion to the capitalisation of the BSE, which currently lists only four companies with total capitalisation of below $400 million.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.93 percent to 84.52 and BLOM stock index rose 2.57 percent to 989.11.
